mainEntity.name: Will my dental implants be damaged by an MRI scan?

acceptedAnswer.text: MRI scans are not expected to damage properly placed dental implants made from standard titanium materials. These materials are specifically chosen for their stability and compatibility with medical procedures. However, always inform MRI staff about your implants to ensure appropriate scanning protocols are followed, and verify your specific implant specifications with your dental team if you are uncertain.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to remove dental implants before an MRI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dental implants cannot be removed for MRI scans as they are permanently integrated into the jawbone. This is also unnecessary since modern implants are designed to be MRI-compatible. The permanent nature of implants is actually beneficial, as there's no risk of forgetting to mention removable dental work.

mainEntity.name: Can dental implants affect the accuracy of my MRI results?

acceptedAnswer.text: While dental implants may create artifacts or distortions in MRI images around the implant area, they typically don't significantly compromise diagnostic accuracy for most medical conditions. Radiologists are trained to interpret images with dental artifacts and can often adjust scanning parameters to minimise interference.

mainEntity.name: What information should I provide about my dental implants before an MRI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Inform medical staff about the number, location, and approximate age of your dental implants. If available, provide documentation from your dental practice including implant brand, materials, and placement date. This information helps ensure appropriate scanning protocols and optimal image quality.

mainEntity.name: Are there any types of dental implants that aren't safe for MRI scans?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most modern dental implants are MRI-safe, but some older implants or specialised systems may contain materials requiring verification. If you're unsure about your implant specifications, particularly for work completed many years ago, consult with your dental team for material confirmation before scheduling MRI procedures.

mainEntity.name: Should I be concerned about pain or discomfort during an MRI with dental implants?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most patients experience no discomfort related to their dental implants during MRI scans. Some may notice slight warming or tingling around implant sites, which is generally harmless. However, report any unusual sensations to MRI staff immediately during the procedure for appropriate assessment and response.
